correctness.rationale: Strict convexity and KKT yield x=y+s J_q(y); invertible two-dimensional Jacobian gives exact p-operator norm of the derivative. Its outward denominator is increasing, straight-segment integration bounds all inputs, and near-boundary derivatives give equality. The p=4 rational function is maximized by calculus at u=1+sqrt(3); the exponent threshold follows by small-ratio asymptotics. Exact integer polynomial check plus 200 pairs and 3 derivative witnesses corroborate critical algebra and finite examples.

value.rationale: This resolves a canonical global stability question for mismatched metric/objective geometry: projecting to the Euclidean disk while measuring error in ℓp. The all-p exact reduction, a non-Hilbert sharp constant (1+2/sqrt(3))^(1/4), and the if-and-only-if nonexpansivity boundary supply motivated information beyond an arbitrary numerical slice.
